**Reasoning** The four candidates are acetate esters of unsaturated alcohols: | Compound | Structure (skeleton) | Characteristic ^1H NMR features | |----------|----------------------|---------------------------------| | **Propenyl acetate** (cis or trans) | CH₃–CO–O–CH=CH–CH₃ | • Acetate methyl singlet (~2.1 ppm)
• Vinyl proton on the carbon bearing the O (deshielded) ≈ 7 ppm, appears as a doublet (J ≈ 16 Hz for trans, ≈10 Hz for cis)
• Vinyl proton on the carbon bearing the CH₃ ≈ 5.5 ppm, coupled to the other vinyl proton (doublet) **and** to the methyl group (quartet) → **dq**
• Methyl on the double‑bond carbon ≈ 1.6 ppm, doublet (J ≈ 6–7 Hz) | | **Butenyl (crotyl) acetate** (cis or trans) | CH₃–CH=CH–CH₂–OAc | Same acetate methyl as above
• CH₂ attached to O appears around 4.5 ppm (not observed)
• Vinyl protons ≈ 5.5–6 ppm with J ≈ 10 Hz (cis) or ≈15 Hz (trans)
• Methyl on the double bond ≈ 1.7 ppm, doublet | The given data: - **7.0 ppm (1 H, d, J = 16.0 Hz)** – a deshielded vinyl proton split only by one neighbour → the proton attached to the carbon bearing the O‑acetate. The large J (16 Hz) indicates a **trans** relationship to the other vinyl proton. - **5.5 ppm (1 H, dq)** – the remaining vinyl proton. It shows a **doublet** from the 16 Hz coupling to the first vinyl proton and a **quartet** from coupling to the three‑proton methyl group. This is exactly the pattern expected for the CH‑bearing the CH₃ in the propenyl acetate skeleton. - **2.1 ppm (3 H, s)** – acetate methyl. - **1.6 ppm (3 H, d, J ≈ 6–7 Hz)** – the methyl attached to the double‑bond carbon, split by the adjacent vinyl proton. No signal around **4.5 ppm** (the CH₂–OAc of a crotyl acetate) is present, eliminating both butenyl acetates. The observed **J = 16 Hz** confirms the **trans** geometry of the double bond. Therefore the unknown is **trans‑propenyl acetate**. **Answer: B**
